newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian OMV aims to boost crude output.
newsitem.headline: Austrian OMV aims to boost crude output.

text.p: Austrian oil and chemicals group OMV AG aims to knock $5 a barrel off its crude oil production costs by the end of 1998 and eventually meeting half of its own refineries' demand for crude from its own output.

Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, director of exploration and production at Austria's biggest industrial group, on Monday forecast crude output would climb towards 80,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the end of 1998 from 60,000 at present.
"Our (longer term) aim is to cover half of our refinery throughput, which means producing roughly 100,000 bpd," said Ruttenstorfer, E&P chief since the start of the month.
Shares in OMV were trading at 1150 Austrian schillings by 1300 GMT, up 17 from Friday's close.

OMV has two refineries -- the 150,000 bpd Schwechat refinery on the outskirts of Vienna and the 60,000 bpd Burghausen refinery in Bavaria, Germany. The firm's crude production is centred in Austria, the North Sea and Libya.
Ruttenstorfer forecast new fields in Libya, west of Shetland and in the Vienna basin, would boost output by up to 20,000 bpd over the next two years.
"And we are on the look-out for another new project by the year 2000...We will invest 1.5-2.0 billion schillings ($137.5-$183.3 million) annually in E&P in 1997 and 1998," Ruttenstorfer said.

"The industry in general is busy investing in up-stream and some firms are putting more than 50 percent of their cash-flow into E&P. There is a lot of money around and competition for good projects is tough," he continued.
OMV's share of production in Libya's Murzuk field, which will come on stream early next year, will start at 3,600 bpd and rise to around 15,000 bpd by 1999.

Total output from the field, which OMV is developing with France's Total and Spain's Repsol, will reach 49,000 bpd in the first quarter of 1997, climbing to 100,000 bpd by the end of the year and 200,000 bpd by 1999, Ruttenstorfer said.

The Schiehallion field, west of Shetland, which British Petroleum Co Plc is developing with Shell, Amerada Hess Corp, Aran Energy, OMV and Murphy Petroleum, should also contribute to OMV's refining independence.
OMV is hoping to pump 5,700 bpd from Schiehallion, which is expected to come on stream in mid-1998.
Ruttenstorfer said the new fields would go some way to cutting OMV's overall production costs from $18 a barrel at present to $13 by the end of 1998.
"An $18 (a barrel) breakeven has plenty of risks attached. Admittedly (benchmark Brent blend) is trading above $20 a barrel now but the price could easily drop in the spring," he said.
"We want to cut the breakeven point to $13 a barrel and that is not the end of the road. Bigger oil companies certainly have more ambitious goals," he continued.

At 1300 GMT, Brent blend crude for January delivery was trading at around $24.09. He said OMV's search for new fields would concentrate on those core areas where the firm was already active -- central Europe, the North Sea, north Africa, Asia and the Far East.
OMV recently made an unsuccessful test drill off the Albanian coast and is considering a second bore. It is also competing for an on-shore licence in Albania and looking for oil in Bulgaria.
Outside Europe, the firm has made a sizeable gas find in Pakistan and has carried out test oil drills in Vietnam.

In the first nine months of this year exploration and production, mired in losses last year, posted 60 million schillings earnings before interest and tax, thanks in part to world oil prices near post-Gulf War highs. ($1=10.91 Schilling)
